action: Treat any unapproved remote-management tool such as a MeshCentral agent as suspicious, review servers for unexpected GitHub, Microsoft Graph, SharePoint or Ably traffic, and load Kaspersky's published indicators into detection.
exec: Espionage tools are hiding inside traffic to trusted cloud services, making them harder to spot with normal network filtering.
org: Government bodies in Asia and Africa
plain: Kaspersky described a spying campaign on government networks in Asia and Africa. Hidden access tools take their orders through GitHub, SharePoint and a messaging service, so the traffic looks like normal cloud use.

key_findings: Victims are in Asia and Africa, mainly government; the worked example is two MeshCentral agent instances inside a Taiwanese organisation.
The entry point is unknown; evidence suggests reuse of an earlier infection, after which the MeshCentral agent was used for DLL sideloading and payload drops.
GitDoor receives commands and uploads results through GitHub accounts created between September 2024 and December 2025, and loads plug-ins and shellcode.
GraphDoor authenticates to Microsoft Graph, keeps encrypted victim data in SharePoint and loads plug-ins for keylogging, screenshots and proxy tunnels over Ably.
Kaspersky sees overlaps with Chinese-speaking FamousSparrow and CopperTurtle but says it cannot definitively attribute the activity.
recommendations: Treat the appearance of legitimate remote-management tools in the environment as suspicious.
Do not rely on network detection alone, since command traffic goes to trusted cloud APIs.
Use the indicators Kaspersky publishes in both parts for hunting.

summary: Kaspersky's two-part report describes Operation ShadowCloud, found in early 2026, against mainly government networks in Asia and Africa. Attackers abused a MeshCentral agent to sideload loaders that run GitDoor, which takes commands through GitHub, and GraphDoor, which uses Microsoft Graph and SharePoint. Plug-ins add keylogging, screenshots and proxies over the Ably messaging service. Kaspersky notes overlaps with Chinese-speaking groups but makes no firm attribution.
title: Operation ShadowCloud: backdoors use GitHub and SharePoint as command channels
